questions.question: The opening of Surah An-Nahl uses the past tense 'ata amru Allah' (the command of Allah has come) to express absolute certainty about a future event, namely the Day of Judgment.
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir and Tabari both explain that the past tense here is a rhetorical device conveying that the Day of Judgment is so certain it is spoken of as already having arrived. The verse immediately warns disbelievers not to hasten it.

questions.question: When verse 3 states that Allah created the heavens and earth 'bil-haqq,' what does this phrase primarily convey about the act of creation?
options: A. That creation took place in six literal days
B. That creation was purposeful and reflects ultimate truth, not random or in vain
C. That creation was completed before mankind was formed
D. That the heavens and earth were created as a test for angels
questions.explanation: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi elaborates that 'bil-haqq' means creation carries inherent purpose and truth, serving as proof of a single wise Creator. Qurtubi adds that purposeful creation points directly to the oneness of Allah.

questions.question: In verse 5, Allah lists the benefits of livestock and uses the word 'dif'.' What does 'dif'' refer to in this context?
options: A. The spiritual benefit of caring for animals
B. The warmth provided by wool and animal hides
C. The sound animals make at dawn
D. The fertility of the earth that sustains livestock
questions.explanation: The tafsir explains 'dif'' as warmth obtained from the wool, fur, and hides of livestock such as camels, cattle, sheep, and goats. Wahbah al-Zuhayli notes that the phrase 'He created them for you' implies not just benefit but a duty of responsible stewardship.

questions.question: Verse 6 of Surah An-Nahl explicitly mentions the aesthetic beauty of livestock, describing the pleasure humans take in seeing them at evening and morning.
questions.explanation: Verse 6 states there is beauty (jamal) in the livestock when they return in the evening and go out to pasture in the morning. Muhammad al-Sha'rawi taught that appreciating this divinely granted beauty is itself an act of gratitude that leads a reflective heart toward worship.

questions.question: The milk verse (16:66) opens with the word 'ibra,' meaning a lesson or sign. What specific miracle does this word introduce?
options: A. That animals were given the ability to recognize their young
B. That pure drinkable milk is produced from between digested food and blood inside livestock
C. That rain causes grass to grow which in turn nourishes both humans and animals
D. That camels can survive without water for extended periods
questions.explanation: 'Ibra' draws attention to the remarkable process by which milk emerges pure and palatable (sa'igh) from between farth (digested matter) and blood inside the animal. Imam al-Tabari described this as each product going to its appointed place — a sign of deliberate divine design.

questions.question: The phrase 'fihi shifa'un lin-nas' in verse 69 about honey is best understood as which of the following?
options: A. It is a drink of moderate sweetness for the pious
B. It contains healing for people
C. It is a provision distributed equally among all creatures
D. It is a sign reserved for those who reflect deeply
questions.explanation: The phrase means 'in it is healing for people.' Imam al-Qurtubi noted that the indefinite form of 'shifa'' suggests comprehensive healing rather than a limited one, while Ibn Uthaymeen emphasized that the healing is addressed to all of humanity, not only believers.

questions.question: The parable of the slave and the free man in verse 71 is used by the Quran to expose the logical inconsistency of polytheism.
questions.explanation: Verse 71 argues that no free man would equally share his wealth with his owned slave, yet polytheists assign divine partners to Allah as though those partners were equals. The verse closes: 'Do they then deny Allah's favor?' Imam al-Tabari identified this as a direct rebuttal of the polytheists' own logic.

questions.question: Verse 90 of Surah An-Nahl commands three things. Which of the following correctly lists all three positive commands in that verse?
options: A. Salah, zakat, and fasting
B. Justice (adl), excellence in conduct (ihsan), and giving to relatives (ita dhi al-qurba)
C. Patience, gratitude, and humility
D. Truthfulness, keeping promises, and forgiving others
questions.explanation: The tafsir of verse 90 identifies three commands — adl (justice), ihsan (excellence), and ita dhi al-qurba (giving to near relatives) — paired with three prohibitions: fahsha (indecency), munkar (wrongdoing), and baghy (oppression). This verse has been recited in Friday and Eid sermons for over 1400 years.

questions.question: The title 'ummah' given to Ibrahim in verse 120 means he led a large nation of followers at that time.
questions.explanation: The tafsir clarifies that 'ummah' here refers to Ibrahim embodying in one person the qualities of an entire community. Ibn Masud, as quoted by Tabari, said that a man who teaches good constitutes an ummah by himself — the word reflects spiritual completeness, not numerical size.

questions.question: Classical scholars Tabari and Ibn Kathir interpreted 'al-ruh' in verse 2 — 'He sends down the angels with al-ruh from His command' — to mean which of the following?
options: A. The soul that Allah breathes into every newborn
B. The revelation (Quran) carried by Jibril to the prophets
C. A special angel separate from Jibril who guards the heavens
D. The spirit of mercy that descends on the night of Qadr only
questions.explanation: Both Tabari and Ibn Kathir explained that 'al-ruh' in this verse refers to revelation — specifically the Quran borne by Jibril — with the core message being tawhid and taqwa. This is reinforced by the closing words: 'warn that there is no god but Me, so fear Me.'

questions.question: According to Ibn Kathir, the phrase 'khasim mubin' (clear adversary) in verse 4 refers to those disbelievers who use the very faculties Allah gave them to argue against their Creator.
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir cited a hadith from Sahih Muslim in his commentary on verse 4, noting the bitter irony that man — created from a humble drop of fluid (nutfah) — becomes a bold and open disputer (khasim mubin) against the One who created him. This is presented as a warning about ingratitude.

questions.question: Imam al-Qurtubi treated verse 43 — 'Ask the people of remembrance if you do not know' — as a Quranic foundation for which Islamic legal principle?
options: A. Ijma (scholarly consensus on new rulings)
B. Ijtihad (individual juristic reasoning)
C. Taqlid (following qualified scholarly authority when one lacks knowledge)
D. Qiyas (analogical reasoning from established sources)
questions.explanation: Qurtubi used 'fas'alu ahl al-dhikr' as a Quranic basis for taqlid — the obligation to refer to scholars when one lacks the knowledge to derive rulings independently. The verse was originally addressing those who doubted prophethood, but its principle of seeking qualified knowledge has broad jurisprudential application.

questions.question: What did Ibn Kathir observe about the grammatical forms Allah uses when addressing the bee in verses 68 and 69?
options: A. The dual form is used, confirming that bees work in pairs
B. The plural masculine form is used, showing bees are communal creatures
C. Feminine singular verb forms are used, which Ibn Kathir noted confirms that worker bees are female
D. The passive form is used throughout, emphasizing that bees act without awareness
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir pointed out that the Quran uses feminine verb forms when commanding the bee — 'ittakhidhi,' 'kuli,' 'usluki' — and noted this aligns with the reality that the working bee is female. This Quranic precision preceded any systematic scientific classification of bee biology.

questions.question: Ibn Kathir cited a hadith from Sahih Bukhari in his tafsir of verse 69 that links honey to healing alongside the Quran.
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir explicitly cited from Sahih Bukhari in his commentary on verse 69: 'Make use of two cures: honey and the Quran.' This hadith grounds the Quranic statement 'fihi shifa'un lin-nas' in prophetic practice and gives it a dual dimension of physical and spiritual healing.

questions.question: According to Ibn Kathir, which companion of the Prophet accepted Islam upon hearing verse 90 recited to him?
options: A. Abu Sufyan ibn Harb
B. Uthman ibn Madh'un
C. Khalid ibn al-Walid
D. Amr ibn al-As
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir recorded that Uthman ibn Madh'un, upon hearing verse 90 recited, was so struck by its moral comprehensiveness that he embraced Islam on the spot. This account illustrates the immediate transformative power this verse had on the early generation.

questions.question: Classical scholars identified three distinct methods of calling people to Islam in verse 125. What are they?
options: A. Recitation, memorization, and transmission
B. Hikmah (wisdom), maw'iza hasana (good counsel), and jadil bil-lati hiya ahsan (debate in the best manner)
C. Patience, gentleness, and firmness
D. Scholarship, public preaching, and private advice
questions.explanation: Verse 125 presents the three-part dawah methodology: hikmah (wisdom suited to the audience), maw'iza hasana (sincere and beautiful admonition), and jadil bil-lati hiya ahsan (engaging opponents with the most excellent argument). The verse closes by affirming that Allah knows best who is guided and who has gone astray.

questions.question: Wahbah al-Zuhayli drew an ecological implication from verse 7, which mentions that livestock carry heavy loads to distant lands. What duty did he derive from the phrase 'He created them for you'?
options: A. That Muslims must prefer livestock transport over mechanical means
B. That the gift of animals for transport entails a human duty of responsible stewardship and care
C. That long-distance trade was specifically encouraged for early Muslim communities
D. That humans are obligated to release domesticated animals into the wild periodically
questions.explanation: Al-Zuhayli noted that 'He created them for you' does not license exploitation but implies accountability — the one entrusted with a gift must care for it. He connected this to broader Islamic principles of environmental stewardship derived from the concept of khalifah (vicegerency).

questions.question: Wahbah al-Zuhayli pointed out that the bee's sophisticated directional communication system was an unknown phenomenon until modern scientific discovery.
questions.explanation: Al-Zuhayli cited the revelation given to the bee in verse 68 as an example of Quranic precision that modern science has begun to uncover. The bee's waggle dance — used to communicate the direction and distance of food sources — was only scientifically documented in the 20th century, yet the Quran's language of divinely guided 'wahy' to the bee anticipates such complexity.

questions.question: Sayyid Qutb described verse 90 as Islam's comprehensive answer to what broader human challenge?
options: A. The challenge of maintaining ritual worship across generations
B. The challenge of building a just and virtuous civilization
C. The challenge of refuting atheistic philosophy
D. The challenge of reconciling science and faith
questions.explanation: Sayyid Qutb wrote that verse 90 offers Islam's complete program for civilizational construction — adl ensures structural justice in society, ihsan elevates individual virtue, and giving to relatives strengthens the family as the foundational unit. He viewed the three prohibitions as the precise forces that destroy civilizations when left unchecked.

questions.question: Sayyid Qutb used the description of Ibrahim as a single 'ummah' in verse 120 to argue that the validity of truth is independent of how many people hold it.
questions.explanation: Qutb wrote that Ibrahim standing alone for tawhid — described as an entire 'ummah' in himself — demonstrates that truth does not require a majority to be true or to have worth. This was a direct response to the modern tendency to judge ideas by popular acceptance rather than conformity to divine guidance.

questions.question: Ibn Uthaymeen interpreted the command in verse 125 to call to the way of the Lord as applying to which audience?
options: A. Only professional scholars and preachers with formal credentials
B. The Prophet Muhammad exclusively, as the verse was addressed to him
C. Every Muslim who possesses knowledge, making this a permanent and universal directive
D. Only those appointed by Islamic governing authorities to the role of preacher
questions.explanation: Ibn Uthaymeen held that while the verse is addressed to the Prophet, its scope extends to every Muslim who carries knowledge. He treated it as a timeless obligation — not restricted to a specialized class — with each of the three methods (hikmah, good counsel, best argument) suited to different audiences and contexts.

questions.question: Wahbah al-Zuhayli connected the description in verse 66 of milk produced from between digested matter and blood to modern physiological knowledge of how mammary glands function.
questions.explanation: Al-Zuhayli noted that the Quran's description of milk emerging from between farth (digestive contents) and blood inside the animal aligns with modern understanding of mammary gland physiology, where nutrients extracted from blood and digested food are processed into milk — an instance of Quranic accuracy preceding human discovery.
